leadIn.title: Lead-In & Context: English Around the World
leadIn.content: English is spoken in many countries with slight variations: American English says 'apartment' while British English says 'flat'.

meaningCheck.question: Function check: What is the primary purpose of using English Around the World?
options: To express clear, level-appropriate meaning in structured context
To translate sentences word-for-word from another language
It is an obsolete form never used by native speakers
meaningCheck.explanation: Correct · This structure provides explicit grammatical function and clarity.

meaningCheck.question: Form check: Does correct usage of English Around the World require matching subject, verb, and modifier agreements?
options: No, agreement rules are optional in English
Yes, matching grammatical forms ensures natural, accurate communication
Agreement only matters in formal academic writing
meaningCheck.explanation: Correct · Accurate form and agreement choices prevent misunderstandings.

form.title: Form & Structure: English Around the World
form.content: Recognizing regional vocabulary and spelling variations (e.g. US: color / UK: colour; US: elevator / UK: lift).

controlledPractice.question: 'I've got a car' most naturally reflects:
controlledPractice.explanation: Have got for possession is the everyday UK form, and is also understood/used in US and Canada.

controlledPractice.question: UK date order for numbers?
controlledPractice.explanation: UK and Australia write dates as day/month/year.
